title: Accelerating Number Theoretic Transform with Multi-GPU Systems for Efficient Zero Knowledge Proof
problem: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), a key bottleneck in zero-knowledge proof generation, has not been efficiently parallelized across multiple GPUs because its butterfly permutation access pattern generates high inter-GPU communication overhead that offsets the compute gains from additional GPUs.
motivation: ZK proof generation is becoming critical for verifiable outsourcing and blockchain applications, and NTT—unlike Multi-Scalar Multiplication (MSM) which has been multi-GPU accelerated—remains the unaddressed bottleneck preventing proof generation from scaling to practical speeds.
method: The paper redesigns the NTT algorithm for multi-GPU execution by restructuring the butterfly computation stages to localize data access within GPU memory and minimize the frequency and volume of inter-GPU data transfers. The approach introduces a GPU-topology-aware permutation schedule that maps NTT stages to GPU assignments so that communication-intensive permutation steps are batched and overlap-optimized with computation. NVLink or PCIe interconnect topology is leveraged to select inter-GPU transfer paths that maximize aggregate bandwidth.
key_novelty: GPU-topology-aware NTT stage mapping that restructures butterfly permutations to minimize inter-GPU communication overhead and enable scalable multi-GPU NTT for ZK proof generation.
contributions: Analysis of inter-GPU communication as the key barrier to multi-GPU NTT scalability.
Topology-aware NTT algorithm that localizes data access per GPU and batches cross-GPU permutations.
Multi-GPU NTT system implementation enabling scalable ZK proof acceleration.
Demonstrated speedup on ZK proof generation benchmarks exceeding single-GPU NTT performance.

metrics.other: Multi-GPU NTT speedup over single-GPU baseline (details in full paper)

limitations: Scalability beyond a small number of GPUs and dependency on NVLink bandwidth are not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: multi-GPU NTT acceleration for zero-knowledge proofs
